target_customer: Software companies and developers that need document data extraction embedded in their products
problem: Extracting accurate structured data from invoices, payslips and other PDFs is slow and error prone for software teams.
product_category: document parsing and data extraction API

founders.name: Alberto Gimeno
education: Computer science and mathematics studies in Spain (school not named)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page. Page says he worked for years as a developer, employers not named.

education: Computer science and mathematics studies in Spain (school not named)

founders.name: Adrian Ramirez
education: Computer engineering and mathematics studies in Spain (school not named)

technical_complexity.rationale: Accurate OCR plus layout parsing across document types was demanding, but cloud OCR services were available as building blocks.

defensibility.rationale: Per-customer learned schemas and SLAs add some lock-in, but large language models later made extraction broadly copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cloud vendors offered OCR as a service; no acquisition or copying of Invofox found. Its own site names Docsumo, Ocrolus and Amazon Textract as comparison points.

market_need_then: Founders say they served several segments until reaching about $1 million in annual revenue, then focused on software companies (founder profile, yespress). No dated spend data found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident, short declarative claims ('No empty promises')

branding.brand_signature: 99 percent accuracy SLA with pay only for correct pages

brand_strength.rationale: Little independent brand coverage; name is distinctive but confusable with similar Invo names in search.

pivots.to: Document parsing API for software companies
pivots.why: Founder profile says they committed to software companies after about $1M in annual revenue (date not stated)

outcome_analysis: Invofox remains active, reports 150 plus software teams and an accuracy guaranteed pay per correct page model, and says it reached about $1 million revenue before narrowing to software companies. Funding is uncertain across aggregators. The main structural risk is that cloud and LLM based extraction made the core capability cheaper to replicate.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights shows $8M convertible note on 2024-02-01 and $10.9M over 5 rounds; Signalbase headlines $11.5M raised; a Caplight page shows a Series A on 2025-02-08 with $14.89M total and an unrelated $16M banner. Investors seen in aggregators include YC, 4Founders, JME, Matt Robinson. No primary announcement found, so no rounds recorded. Founding year conflicts (2015, 2020, 2022). Competitors named on current site are undated; Product Hunt lists API launch 2026-01-29 per a search summary, so none recorded as of 2022. Completeness pass 2026-11: the $8M convertible note II (2024-02-01) is now recorded; it rests on a single database (CB Insights), which totals $10.9M over 5 rounds and lists Y Combinator, 4Founders Capital, Archipelago Next, Lanzadera and others. Total raised exceeds the recorded rounds. Signalbase republishes a company statement of $11.5M new funding with no date or round details, and a Spanish directory claims a Series A, neither confirmed. VCBacked shows a pre-seed in 2022-08.
